thesis: The bear carries the headline-value objection because substantial noncash gains and growing borrowing defeat a simple low-P/E purchase. CFO growth is genuine counterevidence, so the ruling does not infer failed operations or a debt crisis. Recurring post-investment returns must justify the enlarged funding base.
strongest_counterexample: CFO increased from RM1.060bn to RM2.391bn alongside revenue growth, proving some operating improvement is cash-backed and distinct from revaluation marks.
invalidation_conditions: A matched subsequent annual cash bridge shows post-acquisition/maintenance investment and debt-service surplus above zero with borrowings below the observed RM25.353bn, resolving the principal funded-return objection.
Annual CFO below the prior observed RM1.060bn while borrowing remains at or above RM25.353bn would defeat the retained cash-growth counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Recurring earnings excluding fair-value and JV remeasurement.
Acquisition and maintenance outlays, debt service and distributable cash.
Returns on enlarged assets and matched normalised valuation.
decisive_factors: RM855.177m fair-value and RM502.789m remeasurement gains qualify EPS.
Borrowings increased from RM19.590bn to RM25.353bn.
Q4 profit fell; negative trend does not establish an oversold bottom.
